seo.title: Free screen recorder and video editor for Mac
seo.description: Record your screen, camera and mic on a Mac, edit on a multi-track timeline, and let an AI agent do the cuts. Free, open source and local.

sections.title: Record your Mac. Let AI do the cuts.
sections.subtitle: Cameraman records screen, camera and audio as separate tracks, gives you a real timeline editor, and comes with an assistant that edits the video when you ask.
sections.note: macOS 13 or later · Apple Silicon and Intel

sections.title: Everything a screen video needs.
sections.subtitle: Record once, then shape it: cuts, camera, captions, motion and music, all without leaving the app.

items.title: Multi-track recording
items.description: Screen, camera, system audio and microphone are captured at once as separate tracks, so you can trim, mute or move each one on its own.

items.title: A camera that looks good
items.description: Circle, rounded or capsule frames, a blurred, colored or removed background, and a place and size you can change for each part of the video.

items.title: Multi-track timeline
items.description: Trim, split and ripple-delete, then add B-roll, images, color cards and music on their own tracks.

items.title: Auto-zoom
items.description: Clicks and pauses become smooth zooms on their own, and you can still place your own keyframes.

items.title: Subtitles on your Mac
items.description: Speech is transcribed on-device with WhisperKit, turned into styled subtitles, and exported as SRT or VTT. Nothing is uploaded.

items.title: Motion graphics
items.description: Name cards, titles, counting stats and bar charts, or your own HTML animation, rendered to transparent video and placed under the camera.

items.title: Music from code
items.description: Six styles composed on your Mac for the length of the video, ducked under your voice. Or bring your own song.

items.title: Draw while you record
items.description: Pen, arrows, shapes, a laser pointer and blur over the screen, each on a single key.

items.title: Effects per layer
items.description: Sepia, black and white, color, blur and vignette on the screen, the camera or the background, plus voice pitch.

items.title: Export in every shape
items.description: 1080p H.264, HEVC, 4K, vertical 9:16, square, 4:5 and animated GIF, with the mix you set.

items.title: Non-destructive
items.description: Edits live in the project file and your recordings are never changed. Undo anything and move projects as portable bundles.

sections.title: Say what you want. The assistant edits.
sections.subtitle: Open the assistant with ⌘J and ask in plain words. It uses the same editor you do, step by step, and you can watch every change land on the timeline.

points.title: Built into the app.
points.description: One chat for all your projects that runs on your own Claude Code login. Cameraman never sees it.

points.title: 40+ editing tools.
points.description: Projects, clips, camera, subtitles, motions, music and export, over a built-in MCP server.

points.title: Safe to try.
points.description: Edits are non-destructive, so your recordings stay untouched and everything can be undone.

points.title: Bring your own agent.
points.description: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor and Claude Desktop can connect too.

chat.label: Example conversation with the Cameraman assistant
chat.request: Cut the long pauses, add calm music, and show a name card when I introduce myself.
chat.reply: On it. I read the captions to find the pauses and your introduction.
chat.done: Done: 14 pauses cut, calm music under your voice, and a name card at 0:08.

sections.title: From recording to export
sections.subtitle: Download the beta and make your first video in minutes.

steps.title: Download
steps.description: Get the notarized DMG from GitHub and drag Cameraman to Applications.

steps.title: Record
steps.description: Pick a screen, window or area, turn on the camera and mic, and press record.

steps.title: Edit and export
steps.description: Cut on the timeline or ask the assistant, then pick a preset. The file never leaves your Mac.

items.question: Is Cameraman really free?
items.answer: Yes. It is MIT licensed, with no subscription, no account and no watermark. If it helps you, you can support it on GitHub Sponsors.

items.question: What do I need to run it?
items.answer: A Mac with macOS 13 or later, Apple Silicon or Intel. On-device transcription needs Apple Silicon.

items.question: Does it upload my videos?
items.answer: No. Recording, editing, transcription and export all happen on your Mac.

items.question: What does the AI assistant cost?
items.answer: Cameraman charges nothing. The assistant runs the Claude Code you already have, so replies come out of your own Claude plan.

items.question: Is it stable?
items.answer: It is a beta in active development. Recording, editing and export are in daily use; see the changelog for what changed and what is next.

items.question: Can I build it myself?
items.answer: Yes. Clone the repository and open the Xcode project; the README has the steps.
